summary: Kristina Myrvold works in religious studies and Indology. She was a PhD candidate at Lund University, where she also worked as editor, and later became Assistant Professor of Religious Studies at Linnaeus University.

Sinologist and religious studies scholar Kristofer Schipper studied at École du Louvre, EPHE, and Paris Diderot University. His career included posts at EFEO, EPHE, CNRS, Collège de France, Leiden University, and universities in China.

Krisztina Teleki is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. She completed an MA in Tibetan and Mongolian majors at Eötvös Loránd University, where she also served as a research fellow.
Kshanika Saha is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned her PhD at the University of Calcutta, where she studied under Nalinaksha Dutt.

Indologist and linguist Kshetresa Chandra Chattopadhyaya studied under Ganganatha Jha and at the universities of Calcutta, Allahabad, and Sampurnanand Sanskrit. He held appointments at Allahabad University, National Sanskrit University, and Sampurnanand Sanskrit University.

Kshitimohan Sen worked in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies after earning an MA from Sampurnanand Sanskrit University. He worked in the Chamba State Department of Education and long served at Visva-Bharati University, becoming Adhyaksha.

Kumataro Kawada was a philosopher and Buddhist studies scholar who completed his undergraduate and doctoral studies at the University of Tokyo. He held professorships at Japan Women's University, the University of Tokyo, and Komazawa University.

Linguist, sinologist, and Tibetologist Kun Chang studied at Tsinghua and Yale under Franklin Edgerton and Geshe Ngawang Nyima. He held posts at Academia Sinica, the University of Washington, and the University of California, Berkeley.

Kunio Harikai is a scholar of Indology and philosophy who earned his BA and PhD degrees from Kyushu University, studying under Seiren Matsunami and Shoren Ihara. He served as an associate professor at Saga Medical School.
Kunio Iwaya studied at the University of Tokyo between 1963 and 1969 and served on the faculty at Meiji Gakuin University from circa 1977 to 2013.
Kunio Mugitani is a scholar of Sinology, religious studies, and philosophy who studied under Mitsuji Fukunaga. He served as a professor at Kyoto University from around 1993 to 2013.
Kunio Odaka studied at the University of Tokyo from around 1928 to 1931. He later held academic posts at the University of Tokyo and Sophia University.

Kunio Yanagita specialized in Japanology and religious studies, graduating in law from the University of Tokyo. He served in the Ministry of Agriculture and Commerce, on the Permanent Mandates Commission, and held posts at Keio and Kokugakuin universities.
Kuno Fischer was a philosopher who studied at Leipzig University and the University of Halle-Wittenberg. He held academic posts at Heidelberg University and the University of Jena.

Philosopher Kuno Lorenz studied at Tübingen, Hamburg, Bonn, Princeton, and Kiel, earning his habilitation at Erlangen-Nürnberg. He held chairs of philosophy at the University of Hamburg and Saarland University.
Linguist Kuno Meyer studied at Leipzig University under Ernst Windisch. He subsequently held academic posts at the University of Liverpool and Frederick William University Berlin.
Kuntala Bhattacharya works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at Jadavpur University under Amita Chatterjee and Shyamapada Misra, and held a post at Rabindra Bharati University.
Kunzang Namgyal was a scholar who studied under Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thaye and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo.

Kunzang Pelden studied under Patrul Rinpoche, Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso, and Khenpo Shenga. His students included Shechen Gyaltsab, Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, Dodrupchen Rinpoche, and Khunu Lama Tenzin Gyaltsen.

Kurt A. Behrendt works in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He earned his PhD at the University of California, Los Angeles, and served as Assistant Curator in the Asian Art Department at the Metropolitan Museum of Art.
